title: Stomach surgery
what: The surgeon removes part or all of the stomach, or sometimes repairs an ulcer. The esophagus or bowel is joined so food can pass on.
why: For a stomach tumor, a severe ulcer with complications, or bleeding.
duration: surgery usually takes 2 to 5 hours, with 5 to 10 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you have lost weight, and how you are eating

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Nutrition
prepare.text: If you have lost weight, your doctor may prescribe special nutrition before surgery.

bring: Upper endoscopy, biopsy, CT, and test results
Things for a 1 to 2 week hospital stay
steps: You change, an IV line is placed, and stockings are put on to prevent clots
Sometimes a thin tube is passed through the nose into the stomach
The surgeon works through a cut or small openings in the belly
Part or all of the stomach is removed, and the digestive tract is joined
The wound is stitched, and drains are placed
feel: Belly pain. You will get painkillers
Tubes and drains are bothersome, but come out after a few days
You fill up quickly and feel less hungry
after: Drinking and eating start gradually, as your doctor allows
Eat small meals 5 to 6 times a day
Sometimes vitamins and B12 injections are needed. Your doctor will prescribe them
The lab results will guide further treatment
red_flags: Severe belly pain, or a fever over 38°C (100.4°F)
Vomiting blood or black stools: call emergency services
Calf pain, shortness of breath, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I live without a stomach?
faq.a: Yes. Food goes straight into the bowel. You will need to eat often, in small amounts.

faq.q: Why do I feel weak and sweaty after eating?
faq.a: It happens when food moves into the bowel too fast. Small meals and less sugar help. Tell your doctor.

reminders.text: Stomach surgery tomorrow. Bring your test results. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
